title: The Bank of England's fees regime for financial market infrastructure supervision 2026/27
summary: The Bank of England published a consultation paper on April 17, 2026 outlining proposed supervisory fees for Financial Market Infrastructures (FMIs) for the 2026/27 fee year, including an extension to the phased recovery period for UK CCP rulebook costs, with responses requested by May 18, 2026. The document describes how FMI supervision costs fund the Bank's work to ensure financial stability by regulating CCPs, CSDs, and trade repositories. The Bank expects CCP policy activity to reach a more settled state following FSMA 2023 implementation.
key_points: Consultation paper proposes FMI supervisory fee rates for 2026/27 fee year; responses due by May 18, 2026
Extension to phased recovery period for UK CCP rulebook costs is proposed
UK CCP rulebook development under FSMA 2023 is nearing completion; UK CSD rulebook scoping has begun
The Bank expects to begin levying supervision fees for the Digital Securities Sandbox (DSS) in 2026/27
FMI directorate costs have reduced over the past year due to Bank-wide efficiency focus
Responses may be shared with HM Treasury and FCA; all personal data redacted after five years
why_it_matters: This consultation concerns the operational costs borne by FMIs (CCPs, CSDs, trade repositories) for regulatory supervision. While the fees themselves are unlikely to be market-moving, the document confirms the ongoing regulatory transition post-FSMA 2023 and the Bank's approach to onboarding new FMIs including through mobilisation phases. No immediate market catalyst; this is administrative/regulatory in nature.
market_structure_context: While the document relates to Financial Market Infrastructure (FMI) supervision, it concerns regulatory fees rather than actual market structure mechanics, trading mechanisms, or market plumbing. The document confirms ongoing UK CCP and CSD rulebook development post-Brexit but does not detail specific structural changes to market operations.
